findings.evidence:
The reconciliation diff is tautologically equal to `-opening_amount` and never reflects a real écart. Algebraic proof:
  • Controller (CashOverviewController.php:239-242): `$expectedCash = $cashSession->opening_amount + $cashCollectedToday`.
  • Vue (CashOverviewComponent.vue:283-288): `cashDiff = cash_collected - expected_cash`.
  • Substitute: cashDiff = cash_collected − (opening_amount + cash_collected) = −opening_amount.
Empirical confirmation (opening_amount fixture = 100 €):
  • 09 default: collected 58,20 € − expected 158,20 € = −100,00 € (manquant).
  • 09b branch1: collected 58,20 € − expected 158,20 € = −100,00 € (manquant).
  • 02 source=borne: collected 27,40 € − expected 127,40 € = −100,00 € (manquant).
  • 03 mode=cash: collected 58,20 € − expected 158,20 € = −100,00 € (manquant).
  • 05 source=livreur: collected 18,30 € − expected 118,30 € = −100,00 € (manquant).
  • 06 date-range yesterday→today: identical −100,00 €.
Six independent screen captures all show exactly −opening_amount; this is not a coincidence, it is the algebraic identity above. The owner mandate is « détecter écarts (cash manquant) » — but the diff cannot distinguish a healthy drawer from a 100 €-short drawer. The owner-headline KPI shipped is mathematically meaningless. To compute a true écart, the controller must either ingest a counted-cash value (cashier-input) or compute expected_cash as something independent of cash_collected (e.g. opening + cash_collected and compare to an Actual drawer count). The current model conflates Expected and Collected and is unusable for reconciliation.
findings.fix_hint: Two correct shapes: (a) Add a `counted_cash` POST endpoint where cashier records the physical drawer count, then `diff = counted_cash - expected_cash` (where expected = opening + collected); display BOTH counted + expected + diff. (b) For an admin read-only view in V1 LOCAL scope, expose three values without computing a misleading diff: opening / cash_collected_today / 'drawer-count not entered yet — diff unavailable'. Do NOT ship a diff cell whose value is mathematically locked to a fixed identity.

findings.evidence:
The reconciliation `cash_collected` value is polluted by the source / mode UI filter. Empirical:
  • Unfiltered (09 / 09b): encaissées = 58,20 € (= all cash transactions, the true drawer cash IN today).
  • source=borne (02): encaissées = 27,40 € — only borne-cash, NOT the drawer cash.
  • source=livreur (05): encaissées = 18,30 € — only livreur-cash.
  • mode=cash (03): encaissées = 58,20 € (happens to match because filter already restricts to cash).
Root cause: controller line 223 `$summary['by_mode']['cash']['total']` is consumed after the source/mode SQL where-clauses are applied. The reconciliation strip is a property of the cash drawer session itself — physical cash IN does not change based on what the admin filters in the UI. A cashier glancing at 02 may believe the drawer holds 27,40 € today when it actually holds 58,20 €. Combined with C-013 this means filtering source=borne shows a misleading `Écart caisse : −100,00 € (manquant)` despite the drawer being mathematically untouched. Reconciliation must be computed once per request from an unfiltered scope (or from the dedicated CashDrawerSession aggregate), not from the filtered `$transactions` collection.
findings.fix_hint: In CashOverviewController::index, compute the reconciliation `cash_collected` from a SEPARATE query restricted to the drawer's branch + the day, IGNORING the source / mode / branch_id-other-than-drawer UI filters. Alternative: hide the reconciliation card whenever source or mode filters are active (display 'reset filters to view reconciliation'). Either fix dissociates the écart card from the visual filter chrome.

findings.evidence: Below-the-fold rows. Default seed now has 6 transactions (vs round-1's 5) — first 4 rows visible in screenshot, last 2 below the viewport. Aggregate totals verified consistent across all 11 captures: source sum = mode sum = grand total. No data integrity issue; screenshot framing.

The new admin fallback `resolveOpenCashSession` returns the most-recently-opened drawer across ALL branches when admin omits ?branch_id (lines 322-327, orderByDesc('opened_at')->first()). The controller then sees `branchFilter === null` and the reconciliation `cash_collected` calculation path (line 224-237) recomputes cash scoped to that drawer's branch — GOOD. BUT the rendered card shows ONLY the values (opening / collected / expected / diff) without any indication of WHICH branch's drawer is being reconciled. In a multi-branch deployment the admin clicking /admin/cash-overview on a Monday morning would see the reconciliation of WHATEVER branch happened to open its drawer last — could be a different branch than the one being managed. Single-fixture V1 LOCAL won't expose this but it's a P1 footgun for SaaS V2. Owner-grade UI must label the drawer's branch_id next to 'Réconciliation caisse'.
findings.fix_hint: In the reconciliation strip add a labeled span showing the drawer's branch name when admin global view falls back: `Réconciliation caisse — {{ cashSession.branch_name || 'Branche '+cashSession.branch_id }}`. Requires controller to also include `branch_name` in `cash_session` payload (single eager-load on `Branch:name`).
